messages:
mike: Heads-up — our cloud invoice shows the Reserved Capacity (commitment) for prod-gpu-rt being attributed to infra-central instead of the product tags. Saw a spike in infra cost share for March. billing-bot sent a CSV.
julia: omg saw that too. do we have a recent cost export? which tag key are the reserved instances reporting under? :eyes:
billing-bot: Automated alert: 2024-03 invoice parsing detected 1 untagged reservation pool > $120k. Export: s3://billing-exports/2024/03/reservations_unattributed_prod-gpu-rt.csv
mike: Export link is helpful. It looks like a bunch of the legacy reserved pools were created before we enforced the 'team' tag at creation. The reserved resources have 'created_by=infra-admin' and no team/product labels.
sanjay: Quick update from infra: when we migrated the pool provisioning script in 2023 we forgot to carry forward the label mapping. New autoscale pools get tags, but manual reservations still require a tag step. I'll grep the provisioning repo.
emily: For chargeback we rely on two things: (1) resource labels at provisioning and (2) the billing export mapping table (cost_center.csv). If tags are missing we fallback to account-level mapping which is why infra-central is eating the cost. We should avoid retrofitting unless unavoidable.
mike: Short-term ask: can infra annotate the reservation resource objects with 'team' and 'product' where possible? Cloud APIs allow applying tags post-creation for many reservation types (AWS/GCP). Then re-run the cost allocation pipeline for March to see delta.
sanjay: Yep. Plan:
1) Identify reservation IDs from CSV.
2) Attempt tag patch via API for each supported reservation type.
3) For those that don't support post-tagging, add a phantom mapping in cost_center.csv (reservation_id -> team)
4) Re-run allocation job: `python infra/tools/allocate_reserved_costs.py --month 2024-03 --input reservations_unattributed_prod-gpu-rt.csv`
julia: We'll need approvals to change cost_center.csv in the finance repo. I'll file a quick PR once sanjay posts the candidate mapping. Also need a note for accounting about restating March internal chargebacks.
billing-bot: Note: Allocation job supports an override CSV with columns `(reservation_id, team, product, note)`. Use `--override overrides_march.csv`.
emily: Two followups:
- Can we add automated enforcement so new reservations must have `team` and `product` tags? Suggest a pre-provision hook that rejects untagged requests.
- For historical unknowns, do we want to charge infra or split pro-rata across active teams? That's a policy decision.
mike: Policy rec: retro unattributed reservations < $5k -> infra absorbs. >= $5k -> finance run pro-rata across teams using GPU-hours from Feb-March; teams will see a small adjustment. Julia, can finance OK that method?
julia: That approach is reasonable as a one-off. I'll escalate to accounting for signoff. Also propose we send an email to product leads showing the adjustment and the reason.
sanjay: Implementing tags: quick snippet I'll run for AWS reservations (example):
```
aws ec2 create-tags --resources r-0abcd1234efgh --tags Key=team,Value=vision Key=product,Value=embed-rt
```
For GCP comitted use:
```
gcloud compute reservations update my-reservation --update-labels=team=vision,product=embed-rt
```
If the API rejects, we'll add mapping entry.
mike: timeline: can we have candidate mapping by EOD tomorrow? I'll queue the reallocation run on Friday night to avoid interfering with billing jobs.
emily: I'll add a pre-provision check in the provisioning repo as a quick CI hook: fail if `team` or `product` not present. PR tomorrow.
julia: Once we have final numbers, finance will produce a short chargeback report and a GL adjustment ticket if necessary. Heads-up: restatement may affect internal cost dashboards for Q1.
mike: Thanks all. Also let's add a small postmortem after this is done documenting the guardrails so we don't repeat. :thumbsup:
billing-bot: Action items created: #bill-1023 (candidate mapping), #infra-467 (apply tags), #fin-281 (chargeback approval).
